L2t: The sum of divisors of an integer can be found by testing candidates only up to its square root and pairing each divisor i with n/i.
L3t: Sum the proper divisors of each number, starting the total at 1 and leaving out the number itself, by looping i up to sqrt(n) and adding both i and n//i whenever i divides n. Then compare the two sums, so two different primes both give 1 and are treated as equivalent.
L4t: Write a helper that sums the proper divisors of a number (starting at 1, adding i and n//i for each i up to sqrt(n)), and have are_equivalent return whether the helper gives the same value for both inputs.
L2f: The sum of divisors of an integer is usually computed by looping over every number from 1 to n, because divisors cannot be paired up using the square root.
L3f: The divisor sum of a number must include the number itself as well as 1, so each total should be the full sigma value, such as 1+p for a prime p, before the two are compared.
L4f: The function should compute the full divisor sum including the number itself for each input and return whether those two sums are equal.
cand_true: Compare proper-divisor sums (starting at 1, excluding the number itself) computed up to the square root
cand_wrong1: Compare full divisor sums that include the number itself
cand_wrong2: Compare the number of divisors of each integer instead of their sums
